specification.problem: Compute the time-averaged position distribution of a discrete-time coined quantum walk on the N-cycle with a one-qubit memory register coupled to the coin (an assumed model of the recycled-coin walk), and compare it with the uniform distribution via total variation distance, for small N and a grid of memory parameter p in [0,8].
specification.reconstruction_scope: Single smallest instance: N=4 (2 position qubits, 1 coin, 1 memory = 4 qubits), initial state |x=0>|coin=0>|mem=0>, an assumed coin unitary C(p) built from ry(pi p/8) and cx, T steps simulated exactly by statevector, probabilities averaged classically over t=0..T-1. Extensions to N=5..8, other initial states and the Fourier block analysis are listed but not required. The exact recycled-coin operator of the paper and the equivalence proof with the other memory walk are outside scope.

symbols.meaning: rotation angle derived from p (assumed linear map)
coin-controlled shift on position: |x,c> -> |x+(-1)^c mod N, c>
position marginal probability after t steps

equations.label: Assumed angle map
equations.description: Maps the memory parameter p in [0,8] to a rotation angle used by ry in C(p).
equations.justification: Abstract only says p is a real number between zero and eight affecting the coin operator; the linear map is a proposed choice.
assumptions: Linear map; the true paper's coin dependence on p may differ

equations.label: Assumed coin-memory step
equations.description: Illustrative coin unitary: rotate the coin, couple to memory by CX, then swap to recycle the coin into memory.
equations.justification: Sketch suggests ry, cx and a swap-like recycling; exact form is not given by the abstract.
assumptions: Gate order and placement of rotation are a guess

equations.label: Walk step and evolution
equations.description: Coined walk with the shift conditioned on the coin qubit.
equations.justification: Standard coined discrete-time walk structure on a cycle.
assumptions: Shift +1 for coin 0, -1 for coin 1, modulo N

equations.label: Time-averaged distribution
equations.description: Position marginal and its classical average over steps.
equations.abstract_quote: we will consider its time averaged distribution
equations.justification: The abstract names the time-averaged distribution as the studied quantity; the finite-T average is an implementation choice.
assumptions: Finite T approximates the infinite-time limit

equations.label: Deviation from uniform
equations.description: Scalar measure of non-uniform behavior to scan over p, N and initial states.
equations.abstract_quote: only a few produce non-uniform behavior
equations.justification: Needs a quantitative non-uniformity metric; TV is the chosen one.

equations.label: Fourier block decomposition
equations.latex: U\cong\bigoplus_{k=0}^{N-1}U(k),\quad U(k)=D(k)\,C(p),\quad D(k)=\mathrm{diag}(e^{2\pi i k/N},e^{-2\pi i k/N})_c\otimes I_m
equations.description: Translation invariance gives 4x4 blocks in momentum space; eigenphase degeneracies across k explain lack of dephasing.
equations.justification: Standard Fourier analysis of translation-invariant walks; applies to the assumed C(p).

registers.name: pos
registers.size: ceil(log2 N) (2 for N=4, 3 for N=8)

specification.initial_state: |0>_pos|0>_coin|0>_mem (product state at position 0); other coin/memory product states are variations

steps.description: Prepare initial state; for each t from 0 to T-1 compute P_t(x) from the statevector, then apply one step U (C(p) on coin,mem followed by coin-controlled increment/decrement on pos, e.g. QFT adder or modular incrementer; for N=4 use a mod-4 incrementer from standard gates).
Average the marginals over t classically and compute TV against uniform; scan p grid in [0,8], initial states, and N=4..8.
Optionally diagonalize U(k) for each k to check eigenphase degeneracy at special p.

specification.measurement: No measurement in the exact simulation: statevector probabilities are marginalized over coin and memory. If counts are required, measure only pos qubits (bit i of the key from the right is pos qubit i).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Average P_t over t, compute TV from uniform, scan p, N and initial state, and identify the few p values with non-vanishing TV.
assumptions: Memory is one qubit and C(p) is the guessed form of eq_2
Linear map of p to angle
Only N<=8 for the qubit cap; N non-power-of-two needs a modular incrementer on a larger register with unused states left invariant
Time average taken over finite T using exact simulation instead of a phase-estimation time register
